text:
Alex: New user hitting crash when running our sample on Cloudflare Workers. stack: "Cannot find module 'redwood-js-sdk'" at import time.
Lee: Workers only accept pure ESM. Are we shipping a CJS-first package?
Nina: package.json has main -> dist/cjs/index.cjs, module -> dist/esm/index.mjs, types -> dist/types/index.d.ts. But no exports map. That can confuse ESM-only environments.
Omar: Without an exports map, bundlers/packagers may pick main (CJS) and then the worker bundler fails.
Alex: interestingly the local node dev works fine, so the sample misleads onboarding.
Lee: quick fix: add conditional exports so node+bundlers + edge pick correct files. Example suggestion we used before: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./edge": "./dist/esm/edge-shim.mjs"
}
```
Nina: also set "engines" and publish a tiny edge-only entry that avoids node builtins (no fs, no crypto sync apis). Workers/Vercel/Netlify will be happy.
Omar: about types: some folks expect path imports like 'redwood-js-sdk/types' or TS to find types via top-level "types" key. We should keep "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts" at top-level and make sure dts do not import from cjs paths.
Alex: there was another gotcha: our ESM bundle for edge inlined the retry wrapper from node runtime which depends on setImmediate; Workers don't have that, so auth retry didn't work and some requests 401'ed and never retried.
Lee: we need a single auth core that both runtime entries import, but the core itself must be isomorphic (use setTimeout instead of setImmediate, avoid process.nextTick).
Nina: propose structure in repo: src/auth/core.ts -> builds into dist/auth/core.mjs + dist/auth/core.cjs. Then both index bundles import './auth/core'. That ensures parity.
Omar: build pipeline note: our current rollup config produced two fully-bundled outputs with duplicated logic. Switch to externalizing auth/core during bundle step so we get a small shared file.
Alex: short-term onboarding workaround: update sample README and add guarded import snippet: 
```js
const isEdge = typeof globalThis?.WebSocket !== 'undefined' && process.env.CF_WORKER === '1';
const path = isEdge ? 'redwood-js-sdk/edge' : 'redwood-js-sdk';
const SDK = await import(path);
```
Lee: plus a tiny postinstall notice for users using pnpm: pnpm sometimes prefers the module field differently if exports absent. Testing with pnpm, yarn, npm in CI is helpful.
Nina: I'll draft the package.json exports change and an edge-shim entry that is extremely small (only fetch wrapper + auth core).
Omar: I'll rework rollup/tsup to externalize auth/core and ensure types build references the same public API surface. Also add a dts rollup so index.d.ts is clean.
Alex: can someone add CI smoke that runs the sample in a Workers-like env? wrangler dev or vercel dev in CI with a lightweight test would catch this before onboarding.
CI-bot: CI task queued: devex/edge-smoke/sample-runner.
Nina: assigning PRs: I will open export/edge-entry PR. Omar please take build changes. Lee will add README snippet and pnpm note. Alex will own CI smoke.
Omar: also, we should document subpath imports explicitly: tell integrators about '/edge' and recommend consumers prefer ESM imports for edge.
Lee: and add a lint rule in SDK repo to fail if any ESM entry imports node-only modules. We had a handful of regressions that slipped by.
Alex: thanks team, this should reduce onboarding friction and make dual-publish parity less error-prone. I'll follow up after the PRs land.
CI-bot: added labels: devex, sdk, edge, exports, types.
